outcome: Maternal outcome (severe anemia, non-severe preeclampsia, proper antenatal registration)
Perinatal outcome (perinatal mortality, preterm births, low birth weight, admission to neonatal unit/neonatal ICU)
cohort: The study included 212 pregnant women beyond the period of viability, delivering at SKMCH, Muzaffarpur, Bihar, irrespective of live or stillborn outcomes.
finding: Interpregnancy intervals of <= 24 months were associated with higher rates of severe anemia, non-severe preeclampsia, and worse perinatal outcomes including increased perinatal mortality, preterm births, low birth weight, and neonatal unit admissions compared to intervals > 24 months.
